flaw: Microsoft QDK for VS Code (Q# toolchain): remote code execution, no weakness details published
workflow: Opening a crafted workspace or file in the QDK extension; Microsoft published no weakness details
rationale: No weakness information is public, so none of the three criteria can be assessed.

flaw: qiskit-ibm-runtime RuntimeDecoder: imports the module and class named in a job result
workflow: job.result() decodes the JSON the service returns; needs a compromised or impersonated service
rationale: Dynamic import, a classical mechanism, is applied to the JSON of a job result; code runs in the environment that holds the user's programs, results and credentials.

flaw: Qiskit QPY loader: malformed symengine stream crashes the process
workflow: qpy.load() on any circuit file received from elsewhere, default settings
rationale: The crash occurs inside symengine, a classical dependency, when the QPY loader hands it a stream taken from a circuit file.

flaw: Qiskit QPY <13: sympy-encoded expression is evaluated on qpy.load and runs code
workflow: qpy.load() on a QPY <13 file; a sympy-encoded expression is evaluated on load
rationale: The expression parser of sympy, a classical dependency that evaluates its input, is applied to a field of the circuit file.

flaw: CUDA-Q runtime: out-of-bounds read in a network endpoint, triggered by an unauthenticated crafted request
workflow: A request to the runtime's network endpoint; only when the remote-execution server is deployed
rationale: Memory-safety flaw in the runtime's network code, reached through the remote-execution channel; C2 is conditional because the server is not deployed by default. The bulletin does not name the component.

flaw: Amazon Braket SDK: pickle.loads on pickled_v4 job results fetched from S3
workflow: AwsQuantumJob.result() unpickles pickled_v4 results; needs write access to the result bucket or a tampered response
rationale: pickle, a classical mechanism, is applied to job results downloaded from S3.

flaw: Qiskit OpenQASM 2 parser: unbounded expression recursion
workflow: QuantumCircuit.from_qasm_str() / from_qasm_file() on program text from elsewhere
rationale: Defect in Qiskit's own OpenQASM 2 parser, which is quantum-specific code, so C1 is not met.

flaw: Qiskit QPY loader: recursive ParameterExpression evaluation overflows the stack
workflow: qpy.load() on a file with deeply nested parameter expressions
rationale: Defect in Qiskit's own evaluation of parameter expressions, which is quantum-specific code, so C1 is not met.

flaw: protobuf: MessageSet parsing exhausts memory (Cirq's Quantum Engine client)
workflow: cirq-google decodes Quantum Engine responses with protobuf; needs a malicious or compromised service
rationale: Reached through Quantum Engine responses, but the consequence is a crash of the client process only, so C3 is not met.

flaw: requests: Authorization header re-sent after an https→http redirect
workflow: Job submission by the IBM runtime client, which sends its API token in the Authorization header and declared requests>=2.19 until March 2026; needs a redirecting or impersonating peer
rationale: The IBM Runtime client sends the vendor API token in the Authorization header of the job channel, so the token reaches the redirect target.

flaw: requests: a Session keeps verify=False for all later requests to the host
exposed_sdks: Qiskit IBM Runtime, Cirq, PennyLane, ProjectQ, Strawberry Fields
workflow: Clients reuse one Session for the job channel; a single verify=False call disables verification for the host
rationale: SDK clients reuse one Session for the job channel, so certificate verification stays off for later job traffic to the same host.

flaw: urllib3: Authorization header kept on a cross-origin redirect
workflow: As CVE-2018-18074, at the urllib3 layer (cross-origin redirect)
rationale: The vendor API token in the Authorization header is forwarded to another origin.

flaw: urllib3 1.26.0–1.26.3: HTTPS proxy certificate hostname not verified
workflow: Job channel through an HTTPS proxy whose certificate is not verified; proxy use is a documented but non-default configuration
rationale: Man-in-the-middle on the job channel when it runs through an HTTPS proxy; C2 is conditional because proxy use is not the default.

flaw: urllib3: ReDoS in URL authority parsing
workflow: A redirect to a crafted URL hangs the client; needs a malicious or compromised peer
rationale: Reached through a redirect on the job channel, but the consequence is a hang of the client only, so C3 is not met.

flaw: urllib3: request body (job payload) kept on a 303 redirect
workflow: Job payload re-sent to the target of a 303 redirect; needs a redirecting or impersonating peer
rationale: The request body, which carries the circuit and its parameters, is re-sent to the redirect target.

flaw: urllib3: unbounded decompression chain
workflow: Response decompression on the job channel; needs a malicious or compromised peer
rationale: Reached through responses on the job channel, but the consequence is resource exhaustion in the client only, so C3 is not met.

flaw: urllib3: decompression bomb through the streaming API
workflow: As CVE-2025-66418 (streaming API)
rationale: Reached through responses on the job channel, but the consequence is resource exhaustion in the client only, so C3 is not met.

flaw: urllib3: decompression-bomb limits bypassed after redirects
workflow: As CVE-2025-66418, after a redirect
rationale: Reached through responses on the job channel, but the consequence is resource exhaustion in the client only, so C3 is not met.

flaw: waitress: request smuggling via pipelining (Qrisp job server)
workflow: Any request to a self-hosted Qrisp BackendServer (waitress parses it); only when a user hosts the server
rationale: Qrisp's BackendServer, the job endpoint, runs on waitress; C2 is conditional because it applies only when a user hosts the server.

flaw: waitress: denial of service when a client closes early (Qrisp job server)
workflow: As CVE-2024-49768; a client that closes early stalls the server
rationale: Availability of the self-hosted Qrisp job server; C2 is conditional because it applies only when a user hosts the server.

flaw: liboqs: control-flow timing leak in Kyber/ML-KEM decapsulation
workflow: Every TLS handshake on a connection configured with hybrid post-quantum key exchange
rationale: Key encapsulation on the quantum-safe job channel; the timing leak can lead to recovery of the key.

flaw: oqs-provider: length handling of hybrid keys and signatures (buffer overflow)
workflow: Parsing of hybrid key shares and signatures in such a handshake
rationale: Parsing of hybrid key shares and signatures on the job channel.

flaw: liboqs: HQC indexing error exposes part of the secret key
workflow: As CVE-2024-36405, only if HQC is the negotiated KEM (compiled, not enabled by default)
rationale: Affects the job channel only if HQC is the negotiated KEM, which is not the default, so C2 is conditional.

flaw: liboqs: HQC implicit-rejection design flaw
workflow: As CVE-2024-54137 (HQC disabled by default since liboqs 0.13.0)
rationale: Affects the job channel only if HQC is enabled and negotiated; HQC is disabled by default since liboqs 0.13.0, so C2 is conditional. No patched version exists.

flaw: liboqs: secret-dependent branches in HQC
rationale: Affects the job channel only if HQC is the negotiated KEM, which is not the default, so C2 is conditional.
